  The City of Lynwood participates in the Property Insurance Program including auto, earthquake, and flood

  and Terrorism Insurance Programs with coverage limits of $5 million per loss, $3 million per member, and 10
  million per occurrence, respectively. Due to the cost of earthquake insurance, the City only covers essential

  In prior years, a Los Angeles Superior Court trial court ordered the former Lynwood Redevelopment Agency
  (“RDA”) to pay for plaintiffs’ attorneys’ fees and costs in the sum of approximately $600,000 in connection with
  a case settled in March 2009. The plaintiffs appealed that order and filed their opening brief in the Court of Appeals
  requesting a higher amount. The Lynwood Redevelopment Agency filed a respondent’s brief in October 2010. In
  May 2011, the Court of Appeals issued an opinion reversing the award of attorney fees and remanding the matter
  to the superior court to re-determine the amount of the attorney fees awarded. Activity transpired in the Los
  Angeles trial court at the time of redevelopment dissolution between June 28, 2011 and February 1, 2012
  continuing liability on the former Lynwood Redevelopment Agency. After February 1, 2012, in the redevelopment
  dissolution process under AB X1 26, payment for the plaintiffs’ attorneys’ fees and costs were denied by the
  California Department of Finance. In connection with that denial for payment, plaintiffs filed a petition for writ
  of mandate on November 14, 2014 in the Sacramento Superior Court as Case No. 34-2014-80001977.

  The City of Lynwood, as the Successor to the Lynwood Redevelopment Agency, and Lynwood Housing Authority,
  as housing successor to the Lynwood Redevelopment Agency filed a statement of no position in the Sacramento
  case on December 22, 2014. The plaintiffs stipulated with the County of Los Angeles Auditor-Controller and State
  of California Department of Finance to continue the hearing on the plaintiffs’ writ petition to February 26, 2015.
  On February 14, 2017, the parties settled the latter action, entitled Rogel, et al. v. State of California Department
  of Finance, et al., Sacramento Superior Court Case No. 34-2014- 80001977, which had challenged the denial of
  funding for these RDA obligations: the construction of a specific minimum number of units for use by low and
  moderate income residents; and the deposit of funds in the RDA’s Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund
  (“LMIHF”) that were determined as being owed to satisfy the LMIHF Debt. The February 14, 2017 settlement
  precludes the County Auditor-Controller from objecting to future funding of disputed items, subject to Health and
  Safety Code section 34177, subdivision (l), paragraph (1).

  Budget and Budgetary Accounting

  The City follows these procedures in establishing the budgetary data reflected in the financial statements:

  The City’s basis of budgeting for its major fund groups (General Fund, Special Revenue Funds, and Capital
  Projects Funds) is modified accrual.
  Revenues are budgeted according to when they are both measurable and available. Revenues are considered to
  be available when they are collected within the current period, or soon enough thereafter to pay liabilities of the
  current period. The City considers property taxes, franchise taxes, licenses, and interest associated with the
  current fiscal year period susceptible to accrual if they are collected within 60 days of the end of the current
  fiscal year. Only the portion of special assessments receivable due within the current fiscal period is considered
  to be susceptible to accrual as revenue of the current period. All other revenue items are considered to be
  measurable and available only when cash is received. Expenditures are budgeted according to when the liability
  is incurred, regardless of the timing of related cash flow. The exceptions are debt service, compensated
  absences, claims and judgments, which are budgeted as expenditures according to when the payments are due.

  The following procedures establish the budgetary data reflected in the financial statements:
  The City Council approves each fiscal year's budget submitted by the City Manager prior to the beginning of the
  new fiscal year. Public hearings are conducted prior to its adoption by the City Council. Supplemental
  appropriations, where required during the period, are also approved by the City Council. Budget transfers that
  affect the total appropriations for any fund require City Council approval. Budget transfers within a budget code
  with no change in appropriation are approved by the City Manager only and do not require approval by the City
  Council.

  A budget code could be a program or a division of a department or a department. In most cases, expenditures
  may not legally exceed appropriations at the budget code level for the General fund, and fund level for Special
  Revenue, Capital Projects, and Debt Service Funds.
  Legally adopted budgets for all governmental funds are established on a basis consistent with accounting
  principles generally accepted in the United States of America. At fiscal year-end, all operating budget
  appropriations lapse with the exception of encumbered and continuing appropriations. During the fiscal year,
  several supplementary appropriations were necessary.

  Budgets are adopted for all general, special revenue, capital projects, and debt service funds except for Housing
  Authority Special Revenue Fund, 2019 LRB Capital Projects Fund, HUD 108 Loan Special Revenue Fund,
  Other Grants Special Revenue Fund, Prop 1B Grant Special Revenue Fund, CalHome State Grant Special
  Revenue Fund, and Prop 84 Park Grant Special Revenue Fund.

   NONMAJOR GOVERNMENTAL FUNDS

  Nonmajor Special Revenue Funds:
  Special Revenue Funds are used to account for taxes and other revenues set aside in accordance with the law or
  administrative regulations for a specific purpose.

  HUD Home Program Fund - This fund accounts for revenue received from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban
  Development and the State of California to provide financial assistance for affordable housing programs.

  Prop C Fund - This fund accounts for City's portion of sales tax dedicated to transportation programs.

  RMC Grant Fund - This fund accounts for grant received from the State of California, the San Gabriel and Lower LA
  Riverside and Mountains Conservancy for the improvement of water quality, supply and infrastructure.
  Retirement Fund - This fund accounts for revenue received from property tax levy to cover retirement costs.

  Gas Tax Fund - This fund accounts for Gas Tax revenue received from the State of California to cover costs of street
  maintenance and improvements.

  SB 821 Fund - This fund accounts for revenue received from the State of California for the development of bicycle and
  pedestrian facilities.
  Prop A Fund - This fund is used to record the City's portion of sales tax dedicated to transportation programs. These
  programs include the Dial-A-Taxi service for senior citizens and the handicapped, the trolley system, MTA bus fare
  discounts, and transit route projects/programs.
  Measure R Fund - These funds are used to account for revenues and monies spent on critical transit and highway
  projects.
  Air Quality Improvement Fund - This fund accounts for AB 2766 revenues collected by the State of California on
  motor vehicle license registration fees. Revenues are used solely for the purpose of reducing air pollution from mobile
  sources.
  State COPS Program Fund - This fund accounts for the California statewide sales and use tax allocated by the State
  for local public safety services.
  Sheriff Drug Seizure Fund - This fund accounts for revenue received from the Lynwood Sheriff Department's drug
  confiscations. These monies are used to fund various law enforcement and public safety programs.

  Lighting Maintenance Fund - This is a special assessment fund whereby revenue is received from the County of Los
  Angeles for which an assessment has been charged against property owners' front footage. Monies in this fund are used
  to provide services such as tree maintenance, park maintenance, and capital improvements.

  Landscape Maintenance Fund - This is a special assessment fund whereby revenue is received from the County of Los
  Angeles for which an assessment has been charged against property owners' front footage. Monies in this fund are used
  to provide services such as tree maintenance, park maintenance, and capital improvements.

  Impact Fees Fund - This fund accounts for the fees collected from new developments, which will be used to construct
  public infrastructure.

  Public Art Fund - This fund accounts for the fees collected from new developments in-lieu of the developer placing an
  art piece. Funds will be used for the placement of public art.

  Litter Abatement Fund - This fund accounts for Environmental Service Fees and Street Sweeping Charges for the
  City. This revenue funds a portion of the cost for the Right of Way Division and Stormwater Division.

   NONMAJOR GOVERNMENTAL FUNDS

  Nonmajor Special Revenue Funds (Continued):
  HUD 108 Loan Fund - This fund accounts for loan monies received from HUD to assist in funding the construction of
  a new community center and street improvements.

  Housing Community Development (HUD) Fund - This fund accounts for revenue received from the Federal
  Government's Community Development Block Grant Program. The City utilizes this grant to provide community
  programs such as housing rehabilitation loans, code enforcement, and capital improvement projects.

  Business Improvement District Fund - This fund accounts for special tax assessments imposed on businesses in the
  District to promote various activities within the District.
  Beverage Container Recycling Grant Fund - This fund accounts for grants received from the State of California for
  the purpose of implementing a Beverage Container Recycling Program.

  LA County Park Maintenance Grant Fund - This fund accounts for grant funds allocated by the County of Los
  Angeles for park landscape and maintenance.

  Other Grants Fund - This fund accounts for various grant funds received by the City not included in the other funds.

  Used Oil Recycling Grant Fund - This fund accounts for grants received by the City of Lynwood from the California
  Integrated Waste Management Board to cover costs associated with local or regional used oil collection programs.

  Dupont lead Safety Grant Fund - This fund accounts for funds received to assist in the elimination of lead based paint
  and materials.

  Prop 1B Grant Fund - This fund accounts for funds received from the State for street related projects.

  Justice Assistance Fund - This fund accounts for the financial assistance received from the U.S. Department of Justice
  to be used for supporting a broad range of activities to prevent and control crime and to improve the criminal justice
  system.
  Enterprise Zone Program Fund - This fund accounts for funds to be used for economic development and to promote
  job creation and significant private investment that will assist economically distressed areas of the City.

  Refuse Fund - This fund accounts for the collection of removal of trash and debris. Financing is provided by special
  tax, waste collection and other administrative fees.

  CalHome State Grant Fund - This fund accounts for grants received from California Department of Housing and
  Community development to assist Home program in the City.

  Cannabis Cultivation Fund - This fund accounts for required licenses, charges and zoning verification fee related to
  medical cannabis commercial facilities.

   Internal Service Funds

  Internal service funds are used to account for transactions related to the City's garage department, information
  technology, and for its self-insurance programs. These services are provided to other departments on a cost
  reimbursement basis.

  Garage Fund - This fund accounts for reimbursements from City departments for the cost of upkeep on City vehicles.

  Information Technology Fund - This fund accounts for all information technology costs to the City. Funding sources
  are 50% from the General Fund and 50% from the Water Fund.

  Self-Insurance Fund - This fund accounts for reimbursements from City departments for the cost of insurance
  premiums, claims and administration.

  AGENDA STAFF REPORT

  DATE:  February 2, 2021

  TO:  Honorable Mayor and Members of the City Council

  APPROVED BY: Michelle G. Ramirez, Acting City Manager

  PREPARED BY: Michelle G. Ramirez, Acting City Manager

  SUBJECT:  REVIEW OF BOARD, COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS & ANNUAL
  BOARDS, COMMISSIONS AND COMMITTEES LOCAL APPOINTMENT LIST

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review the Board, Commission and Committees members appointment
  list. Currently, there is one (1) vacancy on the CDBG Advisory Board and one (1) vacancy on the Personnel
  Board. The City Council may make any adjustments to these Boards and Commissions, as it deems
  appropriate, in accordance with the rules outlined in the Maddy Act.

  It is also recommended that the City Council direct staff to post the attached Annual City of Lynwood Boards and
  Commissions Appointment List, according to Maddy Act requirements.

  Background:

  Government Code Section 54970, known as the Maddy Act, requires the City Council to annually, by December
  31st of each year, prepare a list of all regular and ongoing boards, commissions and committees, which are
  appointed by the City Council of the City of Lynwood, with the name of the incumbent appointee, the date of the
  appointment, the date the term expires and the necessary qualifications of the positions. The Maddy Act requires
  that this list be posted at an accessible public location and be available to members of the public.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The City Council appoints citizens to serve on a variety of Boards, Commissions, and Committees that have been
  established under Chapter 2 “Administration” of the Lynwood Municipal Code (LMC). Standing members serve
  at the pleasure of the City Council and each Council Member appoints one (1) person to serve to represent that
  county Member’s interest with the community. Section 2-12.4 “Appointment and Term of Members” of the LMC,
  specifies the appointment and term of members, which states:

  “a. Candidates for appointment to subsidiary public bodies shall be nominated by a council member and
  confirmed by a vote of the council. The appointed and confirmed candidates shall serve on the subsidiary public

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 350 of 365
   bodies to which they have been appointed until the earlier of:

  1. A replacement is presented to the council for confirmation by the appointing councilmember;
  2. The appointing council member's term in office has ended; or
  3. The resignation of an appointee.

  b. Members of subsidiary public bodies shall hold office until their successors are appointed, qualified and take
  office.

  c. Any and all provisions of this code relating to terms of office for members of subsidiary public bodies are
  hereby repealed and shall be governed by the provisions of this section. (Ord. #1584,§1)”

  Section 2-12.1(a)(2) “Absence From Meetings; Removal; Compensation” of the LMC, further states "The city
  council may remove any member of any commission, board or committee at any time and without cause; provided,
  however, that any action of the city council to remove a member of the personnel board from office prior to the
  expiration of his term shall not be effective unless approved by at least four (4) councilmember.”

  Currently, there is one (1) vacancy on the CDBG Advisory Board and one (1) vacancy on the Personnel Board.
  The list is being presented this evening for review and potential nominations of community members to fill these
  vacancies as well as any other adjustments to these Boards, Commissions and Committees, as it deems
  appropriate, in accordance with the rules outlined in the Maddy Act.

  Fiscal Impact:

  There is no fiscal impact. Stipends for the Boards, Commissions and Committees are currently budgeted at a
  total of $50 per member per meeting, which have already been included in the approved FY 2020-21 Operating
  Budget.

  SUBJECT:  APPROVAL OF CENTENNIAL LOGO AND APPROPRIATION IN SUPPORT OF THE
  CITY’S CENTENNIAL CELEBRATIONS

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the following resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  APPROVING THE OFFICIAL CENTENNIAL LOGO AND AN APPROPRIATION TO SUPPORT
  ACTIVITIES RELATED TO THE 2021 CENTENNIAL CELEBRATION.”

  Background:

  Incorporated in July of 1921, the City of Lynwood celebrates its 100th Anniversary - its Centennial year - in 2021.
  In recognition of this milestone, and based on direction from the City Council’s Centennial Ad Hoc Committee,
  staff is requesting that the City Council approve the recommended Centennial logo option and an appropriation to
  support community Centennial activities.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  Centennial Logo
  The City Council’s Centennial Ad Hoc Committee reviewed Centennial logo options intended to be used in
  various formats including, but not limited to, printed and digital publicity materials, documents, commemorative
  items, etc. In preparation for consideration of a logo selection by the City Council, the members of the City
  Council were provided the master list of design options for their preview along with the ad hoc committee's
  proposed recommendation. After careful review and analysis of the logo options, the Centennial Ad Hoc
  Committee is formally recommending options “A” and “B” as presented in Attachment #1 (in order of preference).

  These options are recommended based on their classic and simplified styling, which allows them to be presented
  in multiple styles and formats (full color, single color, black and white, etc.), and across all uses (social media,
  letterhead, pins, flyers, banners, etc.). “Busier” or more detailed options pose challenges when trying to reproduce
  them in different formats and are not recommended.

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 353 of 365
   Centennial Activities Appropriation
  Additionally, and based on ad hoc committee discussions and recommendations, staff is requesting that the City
  Council appropriate $150,000 in funding to support Centennial activities and programming to take place in parts
  of both FY 2020-21 and the first half of FY 2021-22. In discussing community celebration options for this key City
  milestone, the ad hoc committee considered fiscal and COVID environment considerations and is proposing a
  budget it deems reasonable and appropriate under current conditions.

  The general Centennial commemoration activities plan revolves around three (3) major elements - with additional
  supporting activities/programming in development and contingent upon final resource allocations and
  COVID/public safety considerations:

  1. A celebratory event/series to be held the day or weekend of the City’s actual anniversary date of July 16,
  2021. The event will feature a time capsule interment and entertainment (in-person & virtual public
  participation dependent upon COVID regulations in place at time of event) and a possible fireworks display.
  2. Signage, banners, public art and printed materials prominently publicizing the City’s centennial anniversary
  throughout the community.
  3. Supporting activities/programs throughout the calendar year - as commemoration budget, City resources
  and COVID-safety allow.

  It is important to note that all proposed and to be determined activities/events celebrating the Centennial are
  dependent upon several factors. Namely, COVID mandates and limitations in place at the time of any event, as
  well as, limits on City resources (budget and staffing) needed to properly execute any event or activity safely and in

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 354 of 365
   a manner that is of high quality.

  Funding for proposed FY 2020-21 activities are being requested from the Unappropriated General Fund to
  revenue and expenditure accounts to be established by the Department of Finance and Administration
  Services ($61,500 or 41% of the $150,000 total). The balance of requested funding supporting activities taking
  place in FY 2021-22 will be accounted for as part of the proposed FY 2021-22 City budget ($88,500 or 59% of
  the $150,000 total).

  The City has contracted with a marketing firm (La Raiz, LLC) to solicit sponsorships to support Centennial
  activities. It is estimated that a range of $25,000 to $150,000 of the total $150,000 appropriations request can
  potentially be reimbursed through sponsorships and revenues. This can be accomplished by a combination of the
  contractor’s successful solicitation of sponsorships supporting Centennial activities currently in development and a
  portion of the contracted, annual contribution from the City’s waste hauler intended to support City special events.

  Given the information provided within this report, staff respectfully recommends that the City Council approve the
  recommended Centennial logo option and the requested Centennial activities appropriations through adoption of
  the accompanying resolution.

  Fiscal Impact:

  The actions recommended in this staff report will have an impact of $61,500 from the Unappropriated General
  Fund in FY 20/21 to appropriate accounts to be established by the Finance Department and dedicated to the
  processing of revenues and expenditures related to all Centennial commemoration activities. The balance of
  requested funding, $88,500 of the $150,000 total, will be part of the proposed FY 21/22 City budget. Funds from
  expected sponsorship revenues and the contracted contributions to support City special events from the City’s
  waste hauler can potentially reimburse $25,000 to $150,000 of the requested appropriation.

  SUBJECT:  APPROVAL OF NEW CITY MOTTO

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING THE OFFICIAL CITY MOTTO FOR THE CITY OF LYNWOOD.”

  Background:

  Incorporated in July of 1921, the City of Lynwood celebrates its Centennial year in 2021. In recognition of the
  celebration and based on direction from the Centennial Ad Hoc Committee, staff is requesting that the City
  Council consider changing the City’s current motto to one that better reflects today’s Lynwood community.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  In light of the City’s Centennial celebration and the remarkable advancement Lynwood has achieved as a
  community, the City’s current motto, “A City Meeting Challenges ” is outdated and can carry a negative
  connotation. Arguably, the decades-old and current City motto does not accurately reflect our community’s
  progress and its bright future.
  At the request of the City Council’s Centennial Ad Hoc Committee, staff conducted a public competition for the
  submittal of motto options, for consideration by the ad hoc committee. The submittal period concluded in mid-
  November 2020. The ad hoc committee reviewed all public and internal entries and subsequently met to discuss
  the submittals. The intent was to narrow the list down to a few, top recommendations for the City Council body to
  consider and ultimately select one to approve.
  The City Council was previously provided with a master list of the entire set of approximately 80 internal and public
  entries received and reviewed by the ad hoc committee. After careful analysis and consideration of each of the
  entries, the ad hoc committee developed a set of original entries that are based on:
  a. A composite of the spirit and intent of what the motto change seeks to achieve.
  b. The general sentiment of the public entries - while keeping in mind that a quality, memorable motto
  possesses the following characteristics:

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 361 of 365
   A short phrase that captures the City’s values.
  Reminds people of our purpose and what we stand for.
  Is easy to remember and provides a shot of inspiration.

  Given the above, the ad hoc committee recommends the following options for a new City motto (in order of rank) –
  with #1 being the committee’s formal recommendation:
  1. The City of Lynwood…  Strength through Community
  2. The City of Lynwood…  It Begins With Community
  3. The City of Lynwood…  Rooted in Community
  A change to the City’s motto is a critical decision that must receive careful consideration. A motto change should
  be approached and considered through the lens of being a permanent change that significantly affects the City’s
  image. The selected motto will be used on City logos, public signage, letterhead, printed and digital marketing
  materials, the City’s website, etc.
  The City Council is under no obligation to select any of the presented motto options and may even decide on an
  entirely new, original option; cancel the current process with no change; or have staff restart the process. Given the
  information provided within this report, staff respectfully recommends that the City Council approve the
  recommended option through adoption of the accompanying resolution or provide staff with further direction.

  Fiscal Impact:

  There is no fiscal impact.
